sources.title: Pfizer PHQ FAQ
sources.evidence: PHQ-9/PHQ-2 are available via phqscreeners.com subject to its terms; access without formal request is conditional on accepting terms.

sources.title: Pfizer PHQ and GAD availability announcement
sources.evidence: Pfizer states users can access/download PHQ and GAD-7 without copyright restriction and at no charge.
supports: Explicit PHQ/GAD free public access; do not invent a blanket electronic fee requirement

sources.title: Chinese adolescent PHQ-9 IRT study
sources.evidence: 5958 records from 12 Chinese secondary schools; ages 11–19; authors report psychometric properties and gender/education DIF.

sources.title: PHQ-9/PHQ-2 validity in Chinese college students
sources.evidence: 959 college students; PHQ-9 optimal cut-off 11 and PHQ-2 cut-off 3 for this study's criterion and sample.

sources.title: Online PHQ-9 screening in Chinese university students
sources.evidence: 230 completed baseline; 81 received MINI; PHQ-9 cut-off 10 had sensitivity .74 and specificity .85 in this online study.
supports: PHQ university evidence and online performance

sources.title: PHQ-9/GAD-7 diagnostic screening performance in Chinese youth
sources.kind: original research / PubMed and publisher PDF
sources.evidence: 2025 Yunnan study analyzed 2,237 children/adolescents who screened positive in phase one and received gold-standard diagnosis; AUCs were .622–.712 and results showed poor performance. Authors caution that positive-screen-only sampling may raise false positives/lower specificity; single province, ages 10–17 and small subgroups limit extrapolation.
supports: PHQ/GAD diagnostic limitation and sampling constraints

sources.title: GAD-7 large Chinese adolescent sample
sources.evidence: 67,281 adolescents aged 10–17; good internal consistency, unidimensional structure and correlation with PHQ-9; this is not equivalent to strong diagnostic-interview discrimination.

sources.title: WHO-5 WHO publication
sources.evidence: Five statements about the previous two weeks, six-point response scale; publication states CC-BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO.

sources.title: WHO copyright and permissions
sources.evidence: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO permits copying, translation and adaptation for non-commercial purposes; commercial use requires permission; adaptations/translations have license and disclaimer conditions.

sources.title: Chinese WHO-5 student validation
sources.evidence: Study validates Chinese WHO-5 in undergraduate students; authors describe it as early evidence for student application, not a universal adolescent validation.

sources.title: DASS official FAQ
sources.evidence: DASS is public domain; questionnaire and scoring key can be copied without restriction. Interpretation in high-distress/clinical contexts should involve appropriately qualified professionals.

sources.title: Chinese DASS-21 student study
sources.evidence: Chinese students recruited online/offline by convenience sampling; study reports acceptable fit across primary, secondary and university groups, with combined school-level groups.
supports: DASS student evidence and sampling limitation

sources.title: SDQ developer product description
sources.evidence: 25 attributes; parent/teacher forms for ages 4–18; self-report wording for adolescents; versions for 2–4 differ; includes optional impact/follow-up components.

sources.title: SDQ copyright / electronic use
sources.evidence: Paper copying without charge is limited to individuals/nonprofits not charging families; no one except Youthinmind is authorized to create/distribute electronic SDQ versions; translation requires authorization.
supports: SDQ digital, translation and fee conditions

sources.title: SDQ Chinese Hong Kong validation
sources.evidence: Chinese SDQ study recruited 3722 community students aged 6–12 and collected parent/teacher reports; limits direct extrapolation to older students and self-report formats.

sources.title: SDQ Chinese adolescent self-report validation
sources.evidence: 1135 adolescents from five mainland Chinese schools, mean age 15.1; study examined Chinese self-report SDQ against YSR and observed differences from British norms.

sources.title: RCADS permissions
sources.evidence: Free to end users but institutional service use, research, translation, derivatives and EHR inclusion require written permission; public posting and commercial distribution prohibited.

sources.title: RCADS FAQ
sources.evidence: Validated for grades 3–8, typically ages 8–18; youth or caregiver forms; norms below validated age are cautioned; gender-diverse norm limitations disclosed.
supports: RCADS age, informant and norm boundaries

sources.title: RCADS official versions
sources.evidence: Official downloads include 47-item youth and caregiver forms and Simplified/Traditional Chinese forms; permission page must be read first.

sources.title: SCARED instrument profile
sources.kind: university instrument repository citing original study
sources.evidence: 41-item child self-report with parallel caregiver form; 3-point response; described for youth 9–18; sums form subscales/total.
supports: SCARED metadata; validate exact current version

sources.title: SCARED original 1997 scale construction
sources.evidence: Original development article (Birmaher et al.); 1997 instrument version differs from later 41-item revision.

sources.title: SCARED replication 1999
sources.evidence: Replication paper for 41-item child and parent forms; authors report psychometric properties in clinical samples.

sources.title: Chinese adolescent SCARED adaptation research
sources.evidence: Indonesian cross-cultural validation (not Chinese) obtained copyright-holder permission; cited to demonstrate translations are rights-dependent, not as Chinese validation.
supports: SCARED permission requirement context; Chinese validation remains unresolved

sources.title: PSS-10 Chinese university psychometrics
sources.evidence: Simplified Chinese PSS-10 study evaluates psychometrics in Shanghai policewomen, not students; do not treat as a student validation.

sources.title: PSS-10 Chinese college reliability and validity
sources.evidence: Record identifies a reliability/validity study in Chinese college students; full method, version, items and license not verified in this pass.

sources.title: Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index official page
sources.evidence: One-month self-report; noncommercial research/education reprint without charge; commercial use/sponsored research requires licensing; modification requires written permission; request form stated for use cases.
supports: PSQI rights, interval and official metadata

sources.title: PSQI instrument profile
sources.evidence: Adult patients; 19 self-rated items plus 5 bed-partner questions; 7 domains; 4-point ratings.

sources.title: Pearson global permissions
sources.evidence: Pearson product content reuse in organizations/publications requires written permission; adaptation, reproduction or translation of a product requires contacting Global Rights Licensing.
supports: Publisher rights context for SCL-90-R and BDI-II

sources.title: Pearson SCL-90-R telepractice guidance
sources.evidence: Pearson describes permitted telepractice as limited to specified Q-global contexts; other telepractice use requires prior permission.

sources.title: Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS) outcome measure profile
sources.kind: professional society instrument profile referencing ePROVIDE
sources.evidence: Lists SAS as 20 items, self-administered and states license required via ePROVIDE.

sources.title: Pearson clinical assessment permissions and licensing
sources.evidence: Pearson offers permission pathways for reproducing, modifying, electronic medical record transfer, educational display and research; purchase is distinct from permission grants.

sources.title: Pearson Clinical Assessment legal policies
sources.evidence: Publisher position: test reproduction electronically or on paper requires prior written permission; reproduction of norms and electronic processing are controlled.

sources.title: CMU PSS developer scales and permission page
sources.evidence: PSS use permission requests must go through ePROVIDE; submitting a request is free and does not commit to purchasing; non-English translation is translator-owned and permission should be sought from translator; PSS is non-diagnostic and has no cut-offs.
supports: PSS use permission, translation rights and no-cutoff guidance

sources.title: CMU Common Cold Project PSS profile
sources.evidence: PSS-10 and PSS-14 versions are listed; past-month timeframe, five response choices, 10-item scoring with four reverse-coded items are documented; permission requests via ePROVIDE are free and do not commit to purchasing, but still form the stated permission process.

sources.title: University of Pittsburgh Assessment Instruments
sources.evidence: University of Pittsburgh provides an investigator resource page and links its Child and Adolescent Bipolar Disorders program for instruments including SCARED in several languages.

sources.title: SCARED Child Version developer-hosted form
sources.evidence: 41-item child self-report form; instructions specify last 3 months and 0–2 response choices; scoring information and 8–11-year-old administration note are present; PDF identifies developers and University of Pittsburgh clinic. This verifies version metadata, not a general commercial/electronic license.
supports: SCARED form, recall period, version and age guidance

sources.title: 2025 PHQ-9/GAD-7 Chinese youth diagnostic screening study, publisher full text
sources.evidence: The analysis contained 2,237 phase-one screen-positive children/adolescents who received gold-standard diagnosis; AUCs 0.622–0.712. Authors note screen-positive-only inclusion could elevate false positives and lower specificity, and discuss single-province, 10–17 age range, subgroup size, and cross-sectional limits.
supports: Detailed methodological limitations for PHQ/GAD youth diagnostic-performance claim
